Welcome to the team coding fusion 

We are a passionate team representing Raipur in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. For this hackathon, we are diving deep into the Space Mission Design Game challenge, aiming to build an engaging and educational interactive experience.
Our current core strengths lie in Software Development, Coding, and Web Development. We love turning complex space data into functional, interactive platforms.
We communicate primarily in English and Hindi.
summary:
ASTRA-SIM is an interactive, browser-based space mission engineering game built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Stepping into the role of a NASA Mission Architect, players design, validate, and simulate planetary and deep-space missions—ranging from Low Earth Orbit climate satellites to Europa cryo-plume probes.
The game challenges players to balance real-world aerospace trade-offs across five subsystems: mission objectives, launch vehicles, power sources, communications arrays, and scientific payloads. Players must satisfy strict engineering constraints, including launch mass limits, Delta-v trajectory requirements, deep-space communication ranges, and inverse-square solar power drop-off beyond 1 AU.
Once a spacecraft passes real-time Engineering Readiness Checks, players launch an animated orbital trajectory simulation featuring live telemetry logs, solar radiation storms, and data-downlink bottlenecks. Built using HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, and the Canvas API, ASTRA-SIM transforms complex space systems engineering into an accessible, hands-on educational experience
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

ASTRA-SIM (Mission Architect) is an interactive, browser-based aerospace systems engineering simulation game where players design, validate, and launch end-to-end NASA space missions.

Players act as a NASA Mission Architect and configure a spacecraft across five interconnected subsystems:

  1. Mission Objective & Orbit: Choose between four real-world destinations—Low Earth Orbit (Earth Climate Observatory), Lunar South Pole Orbiter, Mars Atmospheric & Surface Probe, or Europa Cryo-Plume Flyby—each with authentic Astronomical Unit (AU) distances, Delta-v requirements, and radiation levels.
  2. Launch Vehicle: Select from four rockets (Small-Lift Vector up to Super-Heavy SLS) based on payload mass capacity and Delta-v output.
  3. Spacecraft Bus & Power: Balance standard solar arrays, deployable mega-wings, or Nuclear MMRTG power sources.
  4. Communications & Avionics: Equip S-Band, X-Band, or Ka-Band Optical Laser systems to maintain deep-space signal lock and downlink bandwidth.
  5. Scientific Payloads: Multi-select instruments (Multispectral Imager, Mass Spectrometer, Subsurface Ice Radar, Magnetometer Boom) to maximize science yield.

As selections are made, a real-time Engineering Readiness Check evaluates budget, launch mass margins, Delta-v sufficiency, net wattage at the target distance, and signal range. Once all checks pass, players initiate launch to watch an animated orbital trajectory simulation on an HTML5 Canvas with live telemetry logs, solar radiation storms, data-downlink bottlenecks, and a scored Mission Debrief.

What benefits does it have?

  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Runs instantly in any desktop or mobile web browser with no downloads, installations, or high-end hardware required.
  • Immediate Cause-and-Effect Feedback: Instead of abstract textbook formulas, players immediately see how adding a heavy radar payload reduces Delta-v margin, increases power draw, and demands higher communications bandwidth.
  • Safe Experimentation: Encourages iterative engineering—players can test failed configurations, diagnose bottlenecks using the readiness checklist, and refine their spacecraft until it succeeds.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact of ASTRA-SIM is to demystify space mission design and inspire the next generation of aerospace engineers, students, and space enthusiasts. By turning complex NASA mission trade-offs into an intuitive, hands-on game, the project makes STEM education engaging for classrooms, science clubs, and curious learners worldwide, helping them appreciate the engineering rigor behind missions like Artemis and Europa Clipper.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Coding Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • Graphics & Rendering: HTML5 Canvas API for real-time 60fps orbital transfer trajectories and starfield rendering.
  • Development Software: Visual Studio Code (VS Code) with the Live Server extension for local testing and debugging.
  • Version Control & Hosting: Git and GitHub for open-source code management, and GitHub Pages for live global deployment.
  • Hardware: Standard personal computer/laptop (requiring no specialized GPUs or servers).

How is your project creative?

Rather than building a simple trivia quiz or an arcade shooter, we gamified authentic systems engineering constraints. Our creative approach combines a sleek, dark-mode Mission Control dashboard with dynamic physics penalties—such as inverse-square solar power degradation beyond 1 AU and telemetry bandwidth bottlenecks—so that every design choice creates meaningful strategic tension between cost, mass, power, and scientific discovery.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific & Engineering Authenticity: We modeled real aerospace relationships—such as why solar panels lose efficiency near Jupiter (5.2 AU), why heavy instruments require higher-tier launch vehicles, and why deep-space probes need high-gain Ka-Band or laser communications.
  • Usability & Clarity: We designed a split-screen Mission Control interface where configuration cards sit on the left and live telemetry, readiness diagnostics, and visual feedback sit on the right, ensuring first-time players understand every constraint without needing a manual.
  • Performance & Accessibility: By using lightweight, dependency-free Vanilla JavaScript and CSS Grid, the app loads in milliseconds even on low-bandwidth connections or school Chromebooks.
